_comment: Three-model workload. YOLOv8n period 250.0 ms (4.0 Hz), chosen AROUND its measured single-core service time of 226.9 ms rather than from the plan's nominal 5-10 Hz target -- at 1 core, 4.0 Hz is feasible by service time alone (utilisation 0.91). The sweep exists to locate the boundary, not to manufacture a miss.
_machines_comment: ONE pool of 8, not cpu_p:4 + cpu_e:4. ingest_xpurt_schedule maps CPU_P#n and CPU_E#n to the n-th registry core OF THE NAMED KIND, and every core in cores/spacemit_k1.json is kind 'rvv' -- so with cpu_p_kind = cpu_e_kind = rvv, CPU_P#0 and CPU_E#0 both resolve to cluster0_core0 (hart 0) and cluster 1 is never used. A single CPU_P pool of 8 maps 1:1 onto harts 0-7.
_capabilities_comment: IME is measured, not assumed: smt.vmadot executes on cores 0-3 and SIGILLs on 4-7 (artifacts/k1_bringup/*/ime_capability_probe.txt). It is a property of cluster-0 cores, never a separate machine -- see xpu-rt/capabilities.py. No ModelBlaster kernel targets it today; see artifacts/k1_run/ime_gate/FINDINGS.md.
_topo_comment: topo_tag_override=true pins every machine combination to the single-core profile. singletons + topo_0 must go together: a multi-hart timing here would credit each core with the whole cluster's throughput. ModelBlaster's K1 runner only ever produces topo_<cpu> profiles for the one core it pinned, so topo_0 is what exists.
_fused_full_comment: fused_full (Dima Nikiforov's FusedSensorNet CNN v12: front-camera int8 CNN + ToF-cross int8 conv + low-dim state fuse -> 3-layer LSTM -> 2-D command), pure-int8 build, 13 dispatches, 100% curated-RVV coverage, max_abs_err=0 against the int8 golden on the board. PERIOD 10.0 ms comes from measurement, and from the COLD measurement deliberately. Single-core service time on cpu 0, rdtime at 24 MHz: 92416 ticks = 3.851 ms as a median of 6 warm repetitions, but 183928 ticks = 7.664 ms on the first invocation. The gap is first-touch faulting of the 2.6 MB of const weight arrays and it lands almost entirely on the weight-heavy dispatches (vision_fc 46567 -> 6257, lstm.l0 30087 -> 7925, depth_fc 4111 -> 525). A periodic task has to admit its worst case, so the period covers the cold path: utilisation 0.77 cold, 0.39 warm. The profiled costs the scheduler plans against are the warm medians (worst per-dispatch CV 21.7%). stateful=true is MEASURED, not assumed: the three lstm_s8 dispatches keep h_state/c_state in .bss and nothing resets them, so invocation k consumes what k-1 wrote -- MODELBLASTER_ITERS=3 on the same input gives [12,108], [9,127], [2,127]. Without the flag the scheduler may place instance k alongside k-1 on another hart and they race on one pair of state buffers. num_instances=25 covers 250 ms -- one yolov8_nano period -- not the ~1000 ms the other three span, because a stateful network's instances form a SERIAL chain and greedy's wall time here is strongly superlinear in periodic-instance overlap (417 s at ~1500 ops, 653 s at 1617, 911 s, 1126 s, no result after 40 min at ~1700 ops on the 3-model rungs). 25 instances observes deadline behaviour over a full yolov8 period; it is not a claim about the first second.
